item.title: Configuring Dependency Injection in JAX-RS with Jersey and HK2
item.description:
“Configuring Dependency Injection in JAX-RS with Jersey and HK2”

When building RESTful services using JAX-RS (like Jersey), providing services and managing component lifecycles is crucial. How does one effectively integrate dependency injection (DI) mechanisms, such as HK2 or CDI, to facilitate the injection of services into JAX-RS resources? Various strategies exist, ranging from explicit binding to leveraging container features.

Primary Approach: Defining and Registering an AbstractBinder

The foundational method involves explicitly defining how your dependencies should be instantiated and registered within your JAX-RS application configuration. This utilizes Jersey’s built-in HK2 binding mechanism.

item.title: Jersey CORS Configuration: Implementing Request and Response Filters for API Access Control
item.description:
“Jersey CORS Configuration: Implementing Request and Response Filters for API Access Control”

How does one effectively configure Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) handling within a Jersey-based RESTful application, considering variations between Jersey 1.x and 2.x, and addressing the nuances of simple versus preflight requests?

Setting up CORS correctly is vital for frontend applications to communicate with your backend APIs hosted on different domains. Jersey offers several mechanisms, primarily through container filters.
